item.research_question: How does the addition of Molybdenum (Mo) affect the high-temperature mechanical properties and corrosion resistance of non-equal molar Co-free AlCrFeMnNi BCC high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting of elements with >99.9 wt% purity, ingots re-melted at least three times, forged at 1200 °C with 50% thickness reduction, homogenized at 1200 °C for 6 h followed by air cooling.
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at 600 °C with an engineering strain rate of 10−3 s−1; Potentiodynamic polarization and EIS in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution at 25 °C under deaerated conditions.
key_findings: Vickers hardness of as-homogenized alloys is between HV 350 and HV 400.
Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mo0.1 exhibited a yield strength of 413 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 430 MPa at 600 °C.
Corrosion current density (Icorr) decreased from 3200 μA/cm2 to 61 μA/cm2 with the addition of 0.1 mol Mo.
Corrosion potential (Ecorr) shifted from −340 mV to −60 mV upon Mo addition.
Grain size decreased from 410 ± 101 μm to 284 ± 114 μm with Mo addition.
Nano-scale NiAl precipitates (B2-type) with sizes of 26 nm to 43 nm were observed in both alloys.
The σ phase formed along grain boundaries in the Mo-containing alloy, identified by higher Cr and Mo content.
The impedance of the passive layer (Rpass) for the Mo-containing alloy was significantly higher than the base alloy and 304 stainless steel.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced mechanical strength to slip frustration hardening (SFH) from nano NiAl precipitates and precipitation hardening from the σ phase. For corrosion, the improvement is explained by the formation of a stable MoO3 protective oxide layer in the passive film, which acts as a barrier to electrochemical attack and reduces the dissolution rate of active zones.
item.limitations: The text notes that the σ phase precipitation along grain boundaries leads to intergranular fracture, indicating a trade-off where the Mo-containing alloy exhibits a slightly ductile but more brittle fracture mode compared to the base alloy. Additionally, the authors state that further experiments are required to confirm the specific formation of slip systems and dislocation movement.
item.future_work: Further experiments are required to confirm the formation of the slip system and dislocation movement in Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mox (x = 0 and 0.1) alloys.
quotes: Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mo0.1 exhibited outstanding tensile properties, with a yield strength of 413 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 430 MPa in the elevated tensile test at 600 °C
The corrosion current densities (Icorr) of the Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mox alloy are determined to fall from 3200 μA/cm2 to 61 μA/cm2 as the Mo content increased to 0.1 mol.
MoO3 is a protective oxide layer, which can decrease the rate of the corrosion process, leading to an improvement in the corrosion behavior in H2SO4 solution.
